definitions.explanation: To tear down an existing building and construct a new one in its place.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{家|いえ}を{建|た}て{替|か}える。
{学校|がっこう}を{建|た}て{替|か}える{計画|けいかく}がある。
examples.english: There is a plan to rebuild the school.

examples.japanese: {地震|じしん}で{壊|こわ}れた{建物|たてもの}を{建|た}て{替|か}えるのに{何年|なんねん}もかかった。
examples.english: It took years to rebuild the buildings destroyed by the earthquake.

notes:
{建|た}て{替|か}える is a compound verb meaning to rebuild. It combines {建|た}てる (to build) and {替|か}える (to replace).

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)

NOTE: Do not confuse with {立|た}て{替|か}える (to pay on someone's behalf), which has the same reading but different kanji and meaning.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {家|いえ}を{建|た}て{替|か}える (rebuild a house)
- {建物|たてもの}を{建|た}て{替|か}える (rebuild a building)
